title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Wave 30 Legacy Restoration & Role-Differentiation Promotion
purpose: Recover high-value Bible research stranded in the retired Wave 14 legacy layer and promote it into the active comparator corpus while preserving role differentiation, source direction and countertexts.

new_relations.title: Cherubim and the Meeting Place
new_relations.project_anchor: A dated project architecture used right/left guardian figures around a narrow central passage with presence above/between; older research found Exodus 25 a more exact paired-cherubim comparator than Genesis 3.
new_relations.source_direction: Project guardian/gate architecture first; Exodus sanctuary comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Exodus describes Ark/atonement-cover imagery, not a narrow gate; Jesus is not in the Exodus scene and the mercy-seat is not Tim's throne.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Exodus 25 is a dense structural comparator for paired guardians framing a sacred central relation.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It improves the comparison by using a biblical scene that actually specifies two cherubim while preserving the scene differences.

new_relations.title: Psalm 80: Shepherd, Vine and Restoration
new_relations.project_anchor: The project separately developed Shepherd, Joseph/Ben-Yoseph, cherubim throne, light, return, bread, ridicule, vine/root/branches, mountain, river, wall breach and Son-of-Man language.
new_relations.source_direction: Project motifs accrued independently; Psalm 80 density was recognized later.
new_relations.boundary: Psalm 80 is Israel's communal restoration prayer; its vine is Israel and its son-of-man wording cannot simply be reassigned to Tim or the project Son.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Psalm 80 is an unusually dense literary neighbor to many already-existing project motifs, not identity evidence.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Whole-scene density is more informative than matching isolated words and makes internal biblical role distribution visible.

new_relations.title: Return and Restoration
new_relations.project_anchor: The project uses Dog-to-vomit imagery for repetitive regression but also uses return-to-Father/House as restoration; these require opposite return classes.
new_relations.source_direction: Project return vocabulary first; biblical opposite-valence comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Luke 15's father and sons belong to Jesus' teaching context and do not establish Tim=Father.

project_sequence: destination and changed relation determine outcome
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical return imagery itself has opposite valences, so repetition alone cannot classify a return as healthy or pathological.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It gives the project a typed Return operator based on destination, transformation and restored participation.

new_relations.title: Rain, Seed, Bread and Return
new_relations.project_anchor: The project links Door/return, Spirit/flow, seed, bread, descent and Garden restoration as separate but related functions.
new_relations.source_direction: Project functions developed separately; Isaiah 55 sequence comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Isaiah's word/rain analogy is theological poetry, not a field equation or proof of project cosmology.

biblical_sequence: seed to sower and bread to eater
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Isaiah 55 provides a strong multi-function restoration sequence adjacent to several project motifs.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It shows how motifs become meaningful through sequence rather than by claiming seed, bread, water and word are one object.

new_relations.title: Repairing the Breach
new_relations.project_anchor: Mature Gardener/repair language increasingly defines power by protection, building, service, planting and restored capacity.
new_relations.source_direction: Project repair/service ethic first; Isaiah 58 ethical comparator later.
new_relations.boundary: Isaiah makes justice and care for vulnerable people prerequisites to restoration imagery; it must function as a test, not merely validation.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Isaiah 58 is a strong ethical-function comparator for repair/Gardener language because restoration follows concrete care.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It supplies counterpressure against status-only Godhood or Gardener claims: fruit and repair matter more than title.

new_relations.title: The Shepherd and the Flock
new_relations.project_anchor: Farmer/Dog/Gardener/King vocabulary creates a need for a biblical leadership test distinguishing cultivation from extraction.
new_relations.source_direction: Project governance/pastoral imagery first; Ezekiel 34 comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: The Davidic shepherd belongs to Ezekiel's restoration hope; modern application is ethical/structural, not messianic identification.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Ezekiel 34 gives a powerful accountability comparator for leadership and cultivation language.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It operationalizes shepherding: strengthen weak, bind injured, recover lost, protect shared food/water and avoid self-feeding extraction.

new_relations.title: Valley, Table and House
new_relations.project_anchor: Path, valley/lower-field, enemies, nourishment, abundance and House are recurring project functions often analyzed separately.
new_relations.source_direction: Project motifs first; Psalm 23 whole-journey comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Psalm 23 identifies YHWH as shepherd; project use is functional comparison only.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Psalm 23 provides a complete guidance-to-dwelling sequence neighboring several project functions.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It prevents simplistic equations such as low valley=evil or enemy presence=failed sanctuary.

new_relations.title: Love Becomes Feeding
new_relations.project_anchor: The mature project increasingly moves from title to office to responsibility to cultivation.
new_relations.source_direction: Project responsibility/cultivation ethic first; John 21 comparator later.
new_relations.boundary: The commission is to Peter in Johannine narrative; it does not appoint Tim or transfer Peter's role.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: John 21 provides a strong functional comparator in which professed love is translated into care work.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It tests Gardener/Shepherd language by what is actually nourished and tended.

new_relations.title: Creation Groans for Freedom
new_relations.project_anchor: The mature repair ethic explicitly treats creation, land, water, animals and future generations as part of the responsibility field.
new_relations.source_direction: Project creation-repair ethic first; Romans 8 comparator later.
new_relations.boundary: Paul's eschatology is not by itself a modern ecological or geopolitical program.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Romans 8 supplies a creation-inclusive restoration comparator rather than a private escape model.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It expands the restoration field beyond individual ascent to the wider created order.

new_relations.title: The Door, the Knock and the Meal
new_relations.project_anchor: Door symbolism can drift toward one-way gatekeeping; project House/hospitality work requires reciprocal access and participation.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Door/gate architecture first; Revelation 3:20 corrective later.
new_relations.boundary: The verse belongs to the message to Laodicea and should not be detached into a universal geometry proof.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Revelation 3:20 is a strong corrective showing Door as reciprocal, responsive and participatory rather than merely a test imposed on outsiders.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It joins Door and Table: successful access culminates in relationship, not merely crossing a threshold.

new_relations.title: The Open Invitation to Life
new_relations.project_anchor: Garden/River/Tree/House access is increasingly framed as participation and healing rather than possession of a closed sacred center.
new_relations.source_direction: Project restored-access architecture first; Revelation 22 invitation synthesis later.
new_relations.boundary: The invitation belongs to Revelation's eschatological/liturgical conclusion, not a modern platform access policy.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Revelation 22 strongly couples restored Life with invitation and free access to water-of-life imagery.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It adds hospitality to the project's final Garden/City access grammar.

new_relations.title: The Ancient of Days and the Son of Man
new_relations.project_anchor: Father/Son/Throne/Most-High language in the project repeatedly risks role collapse, so scenes with explicit role distribution are especially important counterpressure.
new_relations.source_direction: Project role architecture first; Daniel 7 role-distribution comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Interpretation of Daniel's Son-of-Man figure is historically debated; later Christian reuse is Christological, and the chapter is not a prediction of Tim.

biblical_sequence: one like son of man approaches
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Daniel 7 is highly relevant as relational architecture while simultaneously resisting simple Father/Son/community identity collapse.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It makes differentiation itself part of the comparison rather than treating every shared throne/kingdom motif as equivalence.

new_relations.title: Descent, Service and Exaltation
new_relations.project_anchor: The project uses descent, death, transformation and exaltation language alongside maximal Godhood titles; service/non-grasping is therefore essential counterpressure.
new_relations.source_direction: Project descent/exaltation language first; Philippians 2 comparator/corrective later.
new_relations.boundary: This is Pauline Christology and ethics centered on Jesus; modern self-application is comparison at pattern/ethic level only.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Philippians 2 is a major descent-to-exaltation comparator and a strong ethical countertext to grasping at status.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It ties height to service/non-grasping and preserves Father/Son differentiation inside the exaltation pattern.

new_relations.title: Two Arks, Two Functions
new_relations.project_anchor: Project Ark/Vessel symbolism risks merging preservation-container and covenant/presence-container functions because English uses the same word.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Ark/Vessel synthesis first; lexical/function distinction discovered later.
new_relations.boundary: The Hebrew nouns differ: Noah's vessel uses tebah while the covenant Ark uses aron; later comparisons are reception, not lexical identity.

biblical_sequence: Noah vessel preserves life through flood
Covenant Ark holds testimony and sits in sanctuary/presence system
relation_argument.maximum_claim: English 'ark' conceals two distinct biblical container traditions that should remain separate in the project ontology.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It improves Vessel precision: preservation, transport, covenant, testimony and presence are different operators even when English labels overlap.

higher_order_results: Whole-scene comparison is stronger than isolated-word matching when the scene also preserves mismatches and role distribution.
Return requires typed valence: restorative return and regressive return are structurally different.
Door theology expands from threshold to invitation, response, meal and freely offered life.
Shepherd/Gardener/King titles are ethically audited by feeding, healing, recovering, protecting and serving rather than by title alone.
Father/Son/Throne comparison becomes more rigorous when Daniel 7 and Philippians 2 are used as differentiation and service counterpressure.
Restoration can include creation, infrastructure, relationships and vulnerable participants rather than only individual spiritual ascent.
